## Ctx.startGiveaway() method

Starts a channel giveaway from a single params object.

**Signature:**

```typescript
startGiveaway(params?: IGiveawayParams | null, options?: IGiveawayOptions | null): Promise<unknown>;
```

## Remarks

Data-driven by design (no `<g-giveaway>` block): `sendGiveaway` has no `parse_mode`<!-- -->, so template interpolation adds no value. Requires the bot to be an administrator in the target channel; the installed grammy exposes no typed `sendGiveaway` (neither `api.` nor `api.raw.`<!-- -->), so this validates fail-fast then sends through a structurally-typed raw call (grammy's raw client dispatches any method name at runtime). Fail-fast validation (1+ channels, future integer `date`<!-- -->, positive integer `winners`<!-- -->, non-empty `prize`<!-- -->) runs BEFORE any API call — programmer errors always throw, never fall back. The first channel receives the giveaway message and doubles as the primary `chats` entry. Channel-targeted by design, so this keeps `api.raw` (context-aware `replyWith*` can only reach the current chat).

Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderDice`<!-- -->): failures are classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`<!-- -->, reported to `notifySendError`<!-- -->, and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`<!-- -->, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`<!-- -->). There is no degraded fallback content for giveaways, so after notify+log the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched.

## Example


```typescript
async handleLaunch() {
  await this.startGiveaway({channels: `@mychannel`, date: 1893456000, winners: 2, prize: `iPhone 16`})
}
```
